I confess to Almighty God, to blessed Mary, ever a Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, to all the saints, and to you, Father, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed, through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech the Blessed Mary, ever a virgin, Blessed Michael the Archangel, Blessed John Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the saints, and you, O Father, to pray to the Lord our God for me.
notes: Runs over the page break at xvi/xvii, breaking after `to the holy`. `through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault` set in italic, answering the Latin's italic `mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa`. After which, Kyrie eleison and Christe eleison are alternately sung in the choir
notes: Set across the full measure, turned over nine lines, with the rubric proper in italic and the words actually spoken, and the two Greek acclamations, in roman: roman are `at solemn Masses,`, `Priest,`, `Mayest thou be blessed by Him, in whose honour thou shalt be burnt,`, `Kyrie eleison` and `Christe eleison`; everything else is italic, including the opening `Here,`. `INTROIT` is set in small capitals with a full-size initial I. notes: Centred across the full measure in roman capitals. The heading is in Latin over both columns; the book supplies no English form of it.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Gloria in excelsis Deo, et in terra
english: GLORY be to God on high, and on earth, peace to men of good will. We praise thee; we bless thee; we adore thee; we glorify thee. We give thee thanks for thy great glory, O Lord God, heavenly King, God the Father Almighty. O Lord Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son. O Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father, who takest away the sins of the world have mercy on us. Who takest away the sins of the world receive our prayers. Who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy on us. For thou only art holy. Thou only art the Lord. Thou only, O Jesus Christ, together with the H. Ghost, art most high in the glory of God the Father. Amen.
notes: Two-line drop G in both columns; `LORY` (and Latin `LORIA`) set in capitals. `Amen.` italic. The book abbreviates `H. Ghost`, not `Holy Ghost`. Neither of the first two `Qui tollis` clauses takes a comma before its petition, though the `Qui sedes` clause does. The Latin prints `Rex cœlestis` with the oe-ligature. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf is light: `mercy`, `away` and `only` are thinned but whole, and the terminal `t` of `art` is faint; all read against the facing Latin.
